about: A general political-values test ("compass"): 36 items from openly licensed or public survey instruments, scored onto an economic left-right axis, a GAL-TAN social axis and a secondary populism axis. Items are deliberately NOT about New Zealand election issues (see data/guide/quiz.json for that); parties are placed on the same axes from published expert data and from our own coding of their documents (data/guide/compass-parties.json).

economic.label: Economic left-right
economic.left_pole: Left: state intervention, redistribution, public ownership
economic.right_pole: Right: markets, limited government, fiscal restraint
economic.basis: Hooghe, Marks & Wilson (2002) economic left-right; CHES "lrecon"; Global Party Survey V4.

social.label: Social: libertarian/green-alternative (GAL) to traditional/authoritarian/nationalist (TAN)
social.left_pole: GAL / libertarian: personal freedom, pluralism, openness
social.right_pole: TAN / authoritarian: order, tradition, national culture
social.basis: Hooghe, Marks & Wilson (2002) GAL-TAN; Kitschelt (1994) libertarian-authoritarian; CHES "galtan"; Global Party Survey V6.

populism.label: Populist / anti-establishment attitudes
populism.left_pole: Pluralist: trusts representative institutions, compromise, minority rights
populism.right_pole: Populist: people vs. elite, popular sovereignty, anti-politician
populism.basis: Mudde (2004); Akkerman, Mudde & Zaslove (2014); CSES Module 5 "Democracy Divided?" elite battery; Global Party Survey V8.

direction_key: +1 = agreeing (or feeling positive) moves the respondent toward the right / TAN-authoritarian / populist pole; -1 = reverse-keyed item.

response_values.likert5: -2 strongly disagree, -1 disagree, 0 neither, +1 agree, +2 strongly agree; a skipped item is null
response_values.feeling5: -2 very negative, -1 negative, 0 neutral, +1 positive, +2 very positive; a skipped item is null

scoring.keyed_score: keyed_i = direction_i * response_i   (so +2 always means the right / TAN-authoritarian / populist pole)
scoring.axis_score: axis = 5 * mean(keyed_i over answered items on that axis), giving -10 (left / GAL-libertarian / pluralist) .. +10 (right / TAN-authoritarian / populist)
scoring.min_items_rule: If fewer than min_items on an axis were answered, do not show a point on that axis; show "not enough answers" instead.

uncertainty.method: half-width = max(1.0, 1.96 * 5 * sd(keyed_i) / sqrt(n))  where sd is the sample standard deviation of the keyed item scores on that axis and n the number answered. The floor of 1.0 reflects that even a complete, perfectly consistent set of 5-point answers cannot locate a person more finely than about one unit on a 20-unit axis.
uncertainty.display: Show the point with an error bar (or shaded band) of +/- half-width, and the text "based on n of N items". With all items answered and sd = 0 the band is +/-1.0.

scoring.subscales: Each item carries a "subscale" tag (SECS economic, SECS social, VSA authoritarianism, CSES populism, WVS economic values, CSES out-group, ESS, NZES). A subscale score is 5 * mean(keyed_i) over the answered items with that tag; show it only when at least half of the subscale's items were answered. SECS subscale scores can also be shown on Everett's original 0-100 metric: secs_0_100 = 50 + 12.5 * mean(keyed_i) (equivalent to mapping -2..+2 onto 25..75; a fully "very positive" conservative answer set scores 75, not 100, because the 5-point version compresses the thermometer).
scoring.acquiescence: Within each axis roughly half the items are reverse-keyed (economic 6/6, social 10 TAN-keyed / 6 GAL-keyed, populism 7/1). A respondent who agrees with everything therefore lands near 0 on the economic axis; on the populism axis the CSES battery is mostly protrait, so the app should treat a populism score as indicative only and show it as a secondary axis.
scoring.party_comparison: Parties are scored with the same formula from their coded answers (data/guide/compass-parties.json: coded.axes). Distance between a user and a party on the two main axes is the Euclidean distance in the -10..+10 plane, shown only for axes where both have enough items.
